prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Plutonium (플루토늄) itself — the sovereign of the Plutonium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: early thirties — a poised, graceful face with soft contours; at most faint lines, no deep folds or under-eye bags.
Face — her own: a stoic, unreadable reserve; deep brown skin; gently long oval face; smaller, narrower eyes than usual anime proportion — deep-set eyes, level outer eye corners; low heavy brows; aquiline nose; thin long lips; amber eyes; smoky dark eye makeup.
Body and hair: lean and toned — a slim, firm waist with softly defined vertical abs and lightly sculpted arms and shoulders, a full bust build; sleek slicked-back hair with no bangs, forehead bare; dark gunmetal hair with tips glowing ember red-orange as if warmed from within.
Expression: a level, steady look, mouth closed.
Her element, carried in her design: plutonium: a synthetic silvery metal first made in December 1940 in a Berkeley cyclotron and named, after uranium and neptunium, for Pluto, king of the underworld; warm to the touch from its own decay, a pellet of plutonium-238 glows red-hot by itself and powered Voyager into interstellar space and New Horizons to Pluto; it takes six solid forms before it melts, more than any other element; born for weapons, it carries a heavy past.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — FANTASY
Costume: a high-fantasy royal or warrior costume — plate pauldrons or a gorget, mail or scale over a long tabard or robe, a circlet or crown, a flowing cape; metal ornament and regalia built from the traits above, subtle magical glow along the patterns.
Silhouette: a long coat below the knees with epaulettes, a belt, gloves and tall boots — a crisp, commanding officer's silhouette. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: dull gunmetal grey, self-heated ember red-orange, tarnished olive, deep underworld indigo.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: a prophesied kingdom that does not yet exist: the blank beyond the last planet on an ancient star-chart, a dark stone gate named for the king of the underworld, unfinished star-charts carved into its posts, a road out to where no sunlight reaches, lit only by a lantern that burns with its own heat.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Pu) and atomic number (94) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, corset, bustle, Victorian tailoring, modern material, machinery.
